raw_segments.text: Looky here, Pip. I'm your second father. You're my son. More to me nor any son. I've put away money, only for you to spend.
When I was a hired-out shepherd in a solitary hut, not seeing no faces
but faces of sheep till I half forgot what men's and women's faces woe's like, I see yawn.
I drops my knife many a time in that hut when I was eating my dinner or my supper, and I says,
Here's the boy again, a-looking at me while's I eats and drinks.
I see you there are many times as plain as ever I see you on the misty marshes.
Lord strike me dead, I says each time, and I goes out in the air to say it under the open heavens.
But what, if I gets liberty and money, I'll make that boy a gentleman, and I done it.
Why, look at you, dear boy. Look at these here lodgings of yarn fit for a lord, a lord.
Ah, you shall show money with lords for wagers and beat them.
